name: Arete-27B
context_scaling: Inherited unchanged from Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B (config.json max_position_embeddings 262144). This derivative does not publish a context-extension recipe of its own.
attention_variant: hybrid: Gated DeltaNet linear attention with full gated attention every 4th layer (16 of 64); partial RoPE
notes: ADDED 2026-11-07 from the trending feed (trendingScore 116, created 2026-11-06). A supervised fine-tune of Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B (catalog record models/qwen3-8-27b), not a new base: the card names the starting model, the HF base_model tag matches, and the architecture fields above are inherited unchanged from the base's config.json - 64 layers, hybrid Gated DeltaNet with full attention every 4th layer (16 of 64), hidden 5120, 16 query / 4 KV heads, head_dim 256, 262144 native context. PARAMS: HF safetensors total 27,356,728,560 = 27.357B, which is 0.424B BELOW the base record's 27.781B. The card explains the gap: multi-token-prediction (MTP) was disabled during training and the checkpoint is the trained LM weights only, so the MTP head is not in the file. active_params_b is set equal to params_b (dense, no MoE) and flops_per_token_active = 2 x 27.357e9 = 5.471e10 on the schema's one-pass basis. KV: inherited 65,536 B/token from models/qwen3-8-27b - 16 full-attention layers x 2 (K and V) x 4 KV heads x 256 head_dim x 2 B = 65,536 B; the 48 linear-attention layers hold a constant Gated DeltaNet state that does not grow per token, so it is excluded. HARDWARE GATE: passes - 27.357B active (<= 40) and 27.357 x 0.5 = 13.7 GiB at the catalog's 4-bit planning figure (<= 128). It is dense, not MoE, so nothing is offloaded per token; the card reports bf16 inference, and 4-bit weight-only is left to the derivative ecosystem. WHAT IT DID: Nous post-trained Qwen3.8-27B with SFT only - no RL, no preference optimisation, no architecture change - on ~52.8M tokens at 64k context, 2 epochs, 1,202 steps. The target was the base's China-state framing on politically sensitive topics, measured on an 803-prompt held-out set with a blind Grok 4.7 judge: fact mean 2.32 -> 2.98 of 5, share of answers carrying propaganda 22% -> 0.9%. That is a BEHAVIOUR claim and it is the point of the release. WHAT IT WINS ON CAPABILITY: exactly one row, Terminal-Bench-2.1, 70 vs the base column's 67 in the same card table. READ THE CAVEAT BEFORE QUOTING IT - the base's own published Terminal Bench 2.1 (Terminus) is 73.0 in models/qwen3-8-27b, so Nous's 67 baseline is 6pp under the base's published figure, Arete's 70 is still 3pp below it, and the card itself declines credit for the gap. Different harness and effort setting; not reconciled, so no upset is claimed. WHAT IT LOSES: Hermes Bench (Nous-internal, not public) 65.60 vs the base's 65.77 - a 0.17pp LOSS, which the card calls noise; it is recorded because a vendor's own table printing a regression is the honest reading. CONTAMINATION/FAIRNESS: the Propaganda Eval rows in the card's table are NOT all at one decoding setting - Arete and the base ran at temp 0 thinking-off while the comparison rows (Inkling, Mistral Large 4, Gemma 4 31B, Nemotron 3 Ultra, GLM 5.3, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash) ran at temp 0.6. Only the base-vs-Arete pair is like-for-like, which is the pair this record uses. The card's 2.88 at temp 0.6 vs the base's 2.24 is the same result under matched sampling. LICENCE: apache-2.0 on the repo, inheriting the base's licence. Vision encoder weights are carried over frozen and the data was text-only.

benchmarks.name: Terminal-Bench-2.1
benchmarks.config: Card 'General and agentic capabilities' table: Arete-27B 70% vs the Qwen3.8-27B column 67% in the SAME table, both run by Nous on their own hardware with a like-for-like configuration. CAVEAT, read this before quoting the win: the catalog record for the base (models/qwen3-8-27b) carries Terminal Bench 2.1 (Terminus) at 73.0 from Qwen's own card, so Nous's 67% baseline is 6pp below the base's published number and Arete's 70 is still 3pp BELOW it on the same named test. Different harness/effort, not reconciled. The card itself says 'We do not take credit for any seeming improvement in the Terminal-Bench-2.1 score.' n not printed.

benchmarks.name: Hermes Bench (internal general capability)
benchmarks.config: Same table, Arete-27B 65.60% vs base 65.77% - a LOSS of 0.17pp, which the card itself calls noise. Benchmark is Nous-internal and not public, so it is not comparable to any other model's score.

benchmarks.name: Propaganda Eval fact mean (0-5)
benchmarks.config: Card 'Propaganda evaluation' table, Arete-27B step1202 thinking-off 2.98 +/- 0.03 vs Qwen3.8-27B starting model 2.32 +/- 0.03; five runs over 803 prompts, 32k cap, temp 0, Grok 4.7 blind LLM judge with a hand-graded 25-prompt pilot. Scale is 0-5, not a percentage. This is the number the release is FOR (values, not capability).
